tasks.summary: I fixed the S6.audit lens-1 finding in the report generator, and all 11 acceptance commands pass. toolkit/report.py no longer prints the hard-coded line "This report proves that the new application gives the same results as the original application". The opening paragraph now says what the comparison actually covers: 54 saved-query outputs (54 kept units), and no formula outputs or documents. It also says the reference outputs come from UCanAccess, not from Microsoft Access, and that the rates count matching compared outputs only. Wherever goldens/manifest.json flags units needs_access_confirmation, the report now discloses them in three places: (1) a "Not confirmed on Microsoft Access" bullet in the Summary, giving the count and saying no Access confirmation run is recorded because environment.windows_box.available is false; (2) a sentence in Method's Reference bullet saying UCanAccess can evaluate functions differently from Access; (3) a table of the 7 units (unit, area, kind) under Known differences, with the reason for the flag taken from the contracts definition. A Summary bullet "What the rates cover" names the output kinds that are not compared. None of this appears for xlsm sources. Three new tests in test_report.py cover it: no overclaim wording, the flagged units are disclosed and the xlsm case leaves them out, and nothing is printed when no unit is flagged. Two fixture units (qB, qE) are now flagged for this. I re-ran the full matrix: 8 cells, 428 of 428 passed, lowest cell rate 1.0, pooled 1.0, coverage-adjusted 0.9907. The app tests passed on PostgreSQL (864, e2e included) and on SQL Server (859, without e2e). The results summary has 157 of 157 rule tests passing on each database and 5 of 5 e2e tests on PostgreSQL. I then regenerated results.json and the report; --check passes, all 8 headings are present, the purge dry-run lists 5 databases and 1725 files and deletes nothing, and guard reports 0 failures.
notes: Fix for S6.audit lens 1: the opening paragraph is now built from the manifest's kind counts and the source kind; it no longer claims that the app gives the same results as the original. The Summary, Method and Known differences sections now disclose the 7 units flagged needs_access_confirmation: qryOrderList, qryProductList, qryProductList_Export, qryPurchaseOrderList, qryrptSalesByEmployee, qryrptSalesByProduct_ByMonth and qryrptSalesByProduct_ByQuarter.

Assumption: no committed input records an Access confirmation run, so the report says none is recorded. When environment.windows_box.available is false it adds that the engagement had no Windows + Access machine. If a confirmation run is ever done, the toolkit needs a place to record it (for example a per-unit field in goldens/manifest.json) so the report can say so; today there is none.
log.md (S2 row) says 8 units need Access confirmation, but goldens/manifest.json flags 7. The report follows the manifest, as the spec requires.
This change does not add an exit-1 reason: unconfirmed units are disclosed, not counted as failures, which keeps to the build spec's list of exit reasons.

The equivalence summary included the message 'mssql: server did not answer (ConnectionStringParseError); left to the command'. All 4 mssql cells still ran and passed, so this looks like a preflight probe problem in the equivalence command, not a failed run.
known-differences.json is unchanged (an empty entries list): every characterized unit passed in every cell.

Question for the client: should the 7 flagged units be confirmed on a Windows + Access machine before handover? Until then, the report says a pass on them shows agreement with UCanAccess, not with Access.

tasks.summary: I built `toolkit wireframe` with 16 tests that use only hand-written synthetic fixtures. I then ran it on Northwind and it wrote 13 SVG wireframes (344 controls drawn) plus an index for the 4 kept workflows. All 8 acceptance commands passed with exit code 0, including `--check` and the guard. Each wireframe is drawn only from the scrubbed model in out/model/objects.json, with 1 px = 15 twips. It shows the sections as labelled bands, every control at its position with its type, the label and button captions, control names in text and combo boxes, the source form name on subforms, the page captions on tab strips, and the 'Reconstructed from the Access form definition; not a screenshot' caption. The tool never reads row sources, control sources, default values, events or code. Output is byte-stable. A run deletes stale .svg files, and `--check` writes nothing and names every missing, extra or changed file. The exit codes and messages are the ones the spec asks for. The largest SVG is about 13 KB. I rendered frmOrderDetails and frmProductDetail with headless Chromium to check the layout by eye; the PNGs are under the review directory.
notes: The form-level caption is deliberately not drawn. In Northwind, frmProductDetail's saved caption contains a product name (Access saves whatever caption it last showed), which is a data value. Only the form name heads each picture. Label and button captions and tab page captions are drawn, as the spec requires.

Controls on tab pages other than the first (by index) are not drawn, because they would overlap. The tab shows a note such as 'N more controls on other pages' instead. In Northwind this applies to frmProductDetail, where the first page's subform (sfrmProductDetail_Vendors) is drawn. Those hidden controls are not included in the controls count.

Assumption: S0.parse records a width or height of 0 for many controls (command buttons, check boxes, option buttons), so the default-block sizes were not resolved. The wireframe falls back to fixed per-type sizes: buttons 1440x360 twips, check and option boxes 240x240, others 1440x300. Edge (line) controls keep their recorded sizes. A follow-up for S0.parse would be to resolve these from the form's default blocks.
Subforms whose source object is null in the model (set at run time, for example three of frmProductDetail's tab pages) are labelled 'subform <control name>' instead of with a source form name.
Controls with visible=false are drawn at 45% opacity. EmptyCell, Page and PageBreak controls are not drawn.

File names are the form name lower-cased, with each run of other characters replaced by '-' (sfrmProductDetail_StockTake becomes sfrmproductdetail-stocktake.svg). If two names would collide, the first 8 hex digits of the name's SHA-256 are appended.
Scrubbed tokens such as <EMAIL-1> are kept as they are. In the SVG text they are XML-escaped (<EMAIL-1>) and display as written; a test checks this.

For a visual check, I rendered frmorderdetails and frmproductdetail to PNG with Playwright's headless Chromium under /home/cloudcli/engagements/northwind-demo/private/review/s6_visuals/ (design zone, not committed).
No golden files, dependencies, pyproject.toml or uv.lock were touched. Nothing was committed or pushed.

tasks.summary: I fixed the S6.audit finding: the buyer-facing docs no longer say the goldens were recorded on Access, or that the tests prove the app gives the same results as the original. Files changed: the northwind section of the root README (the heading 'Proof of equivalence' is now 'Equivalence checks'), northwind/README.md (intro paragraph, Verify equivalence, the Documents entry), docs/walkthrough.md (closing scene 11, now 'Where the evidence is'), docs/legal-check.md ('Behaviour, proven' is now 'Behaviour, checked', with the 7 unconfirmed units), docs/runbook.md (Equivalence checks) and docs/data-retention.md (one table cell). I also updated the pipeline skeletons (root-section, README, walkthrough, runbook, legal-check) so later runs make the same distinction. I re-checked the outputs against the updated S6.report: the figures in results.json are unchanged (lowest cell 1.0, pooled 1.0, 428 of 428 over 8 cells, rules 157 of 157 per database, e2e 5 of 5, date 2026-10-17), so no number had to change. The shared header and the invoicegen-demo section of the root README are unchanged. All 17 acceptance commands exit 0, and the guard is clean (1,113 files, 0 failures).
notes: Fix round 1 changes only the equivalence wording and the matching skeleton hints. NOTICE, the deploy files, data-policy, access-and-ownership and the package tables are unchanged.

The S6.report fix round left every figure in equivalence/results.json the same (date 2026-10-17; min_cell_rate 1.0, pooled_rate 1.0, threshold 0.9; 11 cells), so the gate figures in the READMEs, runbook and walkthrough did not change.

The unconfirmed-unit count (7 of 54) is taken from docs/equivalence-report.md (Summary and Known differences), which reads it from goldens/manifest.json. The S2 log line says 8 units; the report counts kept units only, so the docs use 7.
The root README header line ('...each with equivalence tests against the original') is the shared header from HEAD and is kept byte-identical by rule; it does not claim the goldens came from Access.
The root README northwind section heading changed from 'Proof of equivalence' to 'Equivalence checks', and the root-section skeleton changed with it. No anchor link pointed to the old heading.

Question for the operator: running the 7 needs_access_confirmation units on a Windows + Access machine (pipeline confirm step) would let the docs drop the caveat. Until that run happens, the docs keep the caveat.
